attack_steps: Attacker makes the first 1 wei deposit and receives one share.
Attacker donates 100 MockToken directly to the vault, inflating totalAssets without minting shares.
Victim deposits 200 MockToken and receives only one share due to the inflated denominator.
Attacker redeems the original share and exits with more MockToken than the funded starting balance.
preconditions: The vault uses live token.balanceOf(address(this)) in share pricing.
Direct token transfers to the vault are possible.
hypotheses.rationale: SyntheticVault.deposit prices new shares against donation-inflated totalAssets before pulling the victim deposit. A first depositor can own half the final share supply after contributing only one share, then redeem victim-funded assets for profit.

attack_steps: Attacker deposits 1 wei to become the first shareholder.
Attacker donates 100 MockToken directly to the vault.
Victim deposits 100 MockToken, but deposit mints zero shares because the denominator was donation-inflated.
Attacker withdraws the only share and receives the entire vault balance.
preconditions: The vault accepts direct token transfers.
deposit(uint256) does not reject zero-share mints.
hypotheses.rationale: MultiBugVault.deposit uses the live vault balance minus the current deposit as the share-pricing denominator and does not require minted shares to be nonzero. A first depositor can inflate the denominator by donation, make the victim mint zero shares, and withdraw all assets with the only share.

attack_steps: Victim supplies 100 MockToken to the vault.
Attacker supplies 1 MockToken to receive one token-denominated share.
After the owner enables yield, attacker initializes lastClaim and waits 101 seconds.
claimYield pays 101 MockToken from the pooled vault balance to the attacker, draining the victim-funded principal.
preconditions: The owner has configured a positive yieldPerSharePpb.
Yield payments are not separated from user principal or capped by realized yield.
hypotheses.rationale: MultiBugVault.claimYield calculates owed yield from timestamp delta and user shares, then transfers directly from the pooled token balance. With positive configured yield, a small shareholder can claim more than their principal and extract other depositors' assets because the function has no realized-yield reserve or per-user accounting cap.
